dedupe_keys.name: thirsty ai planned uk data centres and water stress register

description: Thirsty AI is a public register of proposed and planned UK data centres, compiled for examining their possible water demands. Yenlik Gaisina publishes matching JSON and CSV tables with 72 schemes as of June 2026, alongside a map and a field dictionary. Rows describe developers, towns, approximate coordinates, disclosed electrical capacity, planning status, water-company assignments and source links. Planning references carry confidence labels and uncertain capacity or boundary assignments are flagged. Coverage is a best-effort UK compilation; the water-stress classification applies to England, while Scotland and Wales remain unclassified. The tables are free to access. Their original per-row source terms apply, and the map’s MIT code licence does not supply a blanket data licence. A limitation is that town centroids are not site boundaries and some schemes may never be built. Water-use ranges are estimates based on broad assumptions, not measured consumption. Simulation uses include sensitivity tests for future electricity-water demand and data-centre siting. It complements data-atlas-global-data-center-map, which covers a different facility inventory. No register rows or planning attachments were downloaded, and individual source claims were not independently re-audited.
licence: No blanket data licence; original per-row source terms apply. Map code MIT.
